AdminService manages installation-wide settings, user management, and resource presets. Only accessible to instance administrators.

## AcceptThirdPartyTerms

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/AcceptThirdPartyTerms`

Accept the terms, as the version shown, for the items named: this installation then downloads them - the releases this control plane pins at once, and the newest daily.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `termsVersion` | string | The version of the text the administrator was shown: one that is not the current one is refused, so nobody accepts a text they did not read. |
| `items` | list of [ThirdPartyItem](/reference/api/types/#thirdpartyitem) |  |

**Response**

No fields: `{}`.

## GetBill

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/GetBill`

What the installation cost in a month, as its cloud's bill says: by day and service, what the month is forecast to end at, and its budget. As the control plane last read the bill - a few times a day (internal/controlplane/domain/bill) - never the cloud itself, where every question to its billing is billed.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `month` | `Timestamp` | The month, as any instant in it (UTC's); unset is the month in progress. |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `month` | `Timestamp` | The month's first instant, UTC. |
| `readAt` | `Timestamp` | When the bill was last read; unset where it never was - no scope (bill_scope), or a cloud that sends none - and then nothing below is known. |
| `currency` | string | ISO 4217; every amount here is in millionths of it. |
| `totalMicros` | string (int64) | The month so far, every day and service. |
| `forecastMicros` | string or null (int64) | What the month is forecast to end at; unset where the cloud has no forecast yet. |
| `budgetLimitMicros` | string or null (int64) | The installation's budget and what the cloud counts against it; unset where it has none. |
| `budgetActualMicros` | string or null (int64) |  |
| `budgetForecastMicros` | string or null (int64) |  |
| `days` | list of [BillDay](/reference/api/types/#billday) | Oldest first. |

## GetCosts

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/GetCosts`

A month of the bill shared out to the workspaces that caused it: the runners' by what each workspace held of them, the volumes' bucket by what its volumes kept. What nobody caused is said apart and never spread: the runners' capacity nobody held, the bucket's bytes no workspace keeps, and the platform's own cost by role and service; and, from those, what the installation costs a day with nobody working (internal/controlplane/domain/finops).

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `month` | `Timestamp` | The month, as any instant in it (UTC's); unset is the month in progress. |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `month` | `Timestamp` | The month's first instant, UTC. |
| `currency` | string | ISO 4217; every amount here is in millionths of it. |
| `workspaces` | list of [WorkspaceCost](/reference/api/types/#workspacecost) | Costliest first. |
| `idleMicros` | string (int64) | What the runners cost that no workspace held. |
| `unstoredMicros` | string (int64) | What the volumes' bucket cost for bytes no workspace keeps: the images, what nothing references any more. |
| `platform` | list of [PlatformCost](/reference/api/types/#platformcost) | Every other cost - the control plane, the proxy, keys, logs - by role and service, costliest first. |
| `standby` | [StandbyCost](/reference/api/types/#standbycost) | What the installation costs a day with nobody working; unset where no day before the reading billed anything. |
| `readAt` | `Timestamp` | When the month's bill was last read; unset where it never was, and then nothing is answered. |
| `trend` | list of [CostMonth](/reference/api/types/#costmonth) | The year up to this month, oldest first, this month last: each month the bill was read in, shared out as this one is. A month never read is not among them. |

## GetInstallationHealth

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/GetInstallationHealth`

Whether anything is wrong with the installation, in one answer: each part from what the control plane already knows of it - its database, the database's archive, the log store, the collector, its jobs, its hosts and the workspaces waiting for one.

**Request**

No fields: `{}`.

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | [HealthStatus](/reference/api/types/#healthstatus) | status is the worst of the checks'. |
| `checks` | list of [HealthCheck](/reference/api/types/#healthcheck) | One per part the installation has: a part it does not have - a database archive on a development stack, a log store where none is kept, a collector that never reported, jobs on a control plane that does not lead - is left out rather than answered for. |

## GetSettings

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/GetSettings`

Every setting of the installation as it is in force, and what each is: its type, its default, its bounds, what it reaches when saved and who writes it (internal/controlplane/settings, the one registry the file, the dashboard and the CLI are made from).

**Request**

No fields: `{}`.

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `values` | map of string to string | Every definition's value in force, by key, as text of its type: what the installation says, or the default where it says nothing. The control plane's own are left out. |
| `definitions` | list of [SettingDefinition](/reference/api/types/#settingdefinition) | Every setting an administrator is shown, in the registry's order. |
| `runningWorkspaces` | integer (int32) | How many workspaces are running now: what a RUNNING_WORKSPACES setting reaches, and what a NEW_WORKSPACES one leaves as it is. |
| `connectedRunners` | integer or null (int32) | How many runners hold their stream to this control plane now: what a NEXT_HEARTBEAT setting reaches. Unset where this control plane cannot tell. |
| `place` | [InstallationPlace](/reference/api/types/#installationplace) | Where the installation runs and what it runs, read-only. |

## ListAuditLog

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/ListAuditLog`

Read the audit log, newest first. There is no RPC that writes one: an entry is written by the operation it records, so a log an API could add to would be one an API could forge.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | [PageRequest](/reference/api/types/#pagerequest) |  |
| `actorId` | string | Each filter is optional and they are combined with AND; an empty request is the whole log, newest first. |
| `action` | string |  |
| `resourceType` | string |  |
| `since` | `Timestamp` | since bounds the listing at the older end; an audit log is read forward from an incident, and the whole of one is not what a page wants. |
| `excludeActions` | list of string | exclude_actions are actions left out: every sign-in of an installation outnumbers what was done on it, and the one action filter can name what to see but not what to look past. |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `entries` | list of [AuditEntry](/reference/api/types/#auditentry) |  |
| `page` | [PageResponse](/reference/api/types/#pageresponse) |  |
| `actions` | list of string | actions and resource_types are every value this installation can record, so a reader building a filter does not have to know them. They come from the code rather than from a DISTINCT over the log: the log is the one table that only grows, and a vocabulary that is empty until something happens is a filter that is empty when it matters. |
| `resourceTypes` | list of string |  |
| `totalCapped` | boolean | total_capped says page.total_count is where counting stopped, not the count: the log is counted up to a bound, since counting all of it is reading all of it on every page. |

## ListTimeline

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/ListTimeline`

What happened, newest first, between two instants, to one workspace, host, team or project, or to the whole installation: read from the audit log, the workspaces' events, the jobs' failed runs and the projects' prebuilds as they are, never copied. Sign-ins and what is done inside a workspace (a session, a command) are the audit log's alone: they outnumber everything else.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `since` | `Timestamp` | Inclusive; unset reads from as far back as the records go. |
| `until` | `Timestamp` | Exclusive; unset is now. |
| `page` | [PageRequest](/reference/api/types/#pagerequest) | page_size is at most 200, and zero is 50. total_count is not counted. |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `events` | list of [TimelineEvent](/reference/api/types/#timelineevent) |  |
| `page` | [PageResponse](/reference/api/types/#pageresponse) |  |
| `keptDays` | integer (int32) | kept_days is how long what the timeline reads is kept (ListWorkspaceTimelineResponse). |

## ListUsers

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/ListUsers`

List all users

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | [PageRequest](/reference/api/types/#pagerequest) |  |
| `query` | string | Optional: filter by name or email |
| `adminsOnly` | boolean | Optional: only return admin users |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | list of [User](/reference/api/types/#user) |  |
| `page` | [PageResponse](/reference/api/types/#pageresponse) |  |
| `holdings` | map of string to [UserHoldings](/reference/api/types/#userholdings) | What each listed user still holds, by user id: what an administrator asks before taking access away. Kept off User, which other calls return without it. |
| `refusedRemovals` | map of string to string | Why removing a listed user as an administrator, or disabling them, would be refused, by user id; absent where it would not be. The refusal is the database's (lockout), so a client that never reads this is refused the same. |

## PublishVSCodeServers

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/PublishVSCodeServers`

Publish the servers of the newest stable VS Code releases, or of the commits named, as a new release. Answers once the publish has begun - it downloads a gigabyte - and GetVSCodeServers says how it goes.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `newest` | integer (int32) | The newest stable releases to carry: 2 is the current one and the one before it. |
| `commits` | list of string | Commits to carry besides, each the second line of `code --version`. |

**Response**

No fields: `{}`.

## RecoverUserWorkspace

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/RecoverUserWorkspace`

Move a workspace off a host that is gone, as its owner's RecoverWorkspace does, and with the same question first: without accept_data_loss it answers what the move would give up and changes nothing. The work given up is its owner's, so a reason is required, kept on the audit entry, and written with who asked on the workspace's history, which its owner reads (WORKSPACE_EVENT_TYPE_RECOVERED_BY_ADMIN). Refused for a workspace held in quarantine.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaceId` | string | The workspace's id. |
| `acceptDataLoss` | boolean | False asks what it would cost. True accepts that cost, for its owner, and does it. |
| `reason` | string | Why: required, kept on the audit entry and on the workspace's history for its owner. |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `recovery` | [RecoverWorkspaceResponse](/reference/api/workspaceservice/#recoverworkspace) |  |

## RekeyVolume

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/RekeyVolume`

Re-key a workspace's disk: copy it whole under a key of its own, point the workspace at the copy, and delete the disk - which shreds the key assumed taken and every snapshot of the disk, since those are what that key opens. The workspace must be stopped or quarantined. Refused for a disk something descends from. Audited.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaceId` | string |  |

**Response**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `targetVolumeId` | string |  |

## RemoveStoredVolume

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/RemoveStoredVolume`

Remove an image, an extension release, an unclaimed volume or an orphan from the store: its row, then its volume, whose key is shredded; storage-gc collects its layers on its next run. Refused for one that is kept (StoredVolume.kept_because), one placed on a host, and a workspace's disk. Audited.

**Request**

| Field | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `volumeId` | string |  |

**Response**

No fields: `{}`.

`POST /spin.v1.AdminService/SendTestAlert`

Has Grafana test its contact point, which sends a test alert the whole way an alert goes: Grafana, the control plane, an email to every administrator who has not opted out. FAILED_PRECONDITION where this control plane serves no Grafana, or Grafana could not reach the control plane.

No fields: `{}`.

No fields: `{}`.
